narrative.h2: Phonk video runs on tire smoke and Memphis ghosts

sections.heading: What phonk looks like
sections.body: Phonk visuals took the 1990s Memphis rap mixtape aesthetic, ran it through TikTok, and added drift cars. The look is heavily compressed: distorted neon, VHS tracking errors, frame ghosting, blown reds. Masked figures appear constantly — balaclavas, demon masks, anonymous silhouettes. Cars are central, almost always sideways. Color is dominated by red and black with occasional acid green or hot pink intrusions. Text overlays in cracked Cyrillic-influenced fonts often appear over the action.

sections.heading: Reference points that actually work
sections.body: Kordhell's 'Murder in My Mind', self-produced like most phonk visuals, set the modern template with car-focused, mask-heavy imagery. PLUSMA's 'Trouble', MoneySamuel, and Pharaoh come from the Russian phonk scene that shaped the current aesthetic. DVRST's 'Close Eyes' carried the drift-and-distortion language to a billion views, and Hensonn's 'Sahara' codified the desert-drift subgenre. Earlier influences run straight back to Three 6 Mafia's 'Tear Da Club Up' and DJ Screw mixtape art. The thread: aggressive lo-fi treatment of every frame, plus a refusal to ever show a clean face.

sections.heading: Prompting tip for Tunee
sections.body: Lean into the degradation. Prompt Tunee for 'heavy VHS noise, chromatic aberration on the edges, blown red highlights, frame skipping every two seconds'. Specify the car early — 'rear-wheel-drive coupe mid-drift, tire smoke filling the lower third'. Faces should be obscured or partial. Add Cyrillic-style text in the corner of the frame for authenticity. Don't ask for clean output. Phonk that looks rendered cleanly loses what the genre is for.
